title: Reading & Writing CSV Data with pd.read_csv() and to_csv()
code:
import io
import pandas as pd

# Simulated CSV string representation of warehouse inventory
csv_text = '''SKU,Item,Category,Price,Stock
101,Keyboard,Electronics,1800,45
102,Notebook,Stationery,120,200
103,Mouse,Electronics,650,80
104,Stapler,Stationery,350,30'''

# 1. Parse CSV into DataFrame
inventory = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_text))
print("Loaded Inventory DataFrame:")
print(inventory)

# 2. Add total inventory value column
inventory["TotalValue"] = inventory["Price"] * inventory["Stock"]

# 3. Export back to CSV string without redundant row indices
output_csv = inventory.to_csv(index=False)
print("\nExported CSV Representation (index=False):")
print(output_csv.strip())
explanation: pd.read_csv() seamlessly converts comma-separated strings or file streams into structured DataFrames. to_csv(index=False) serializes the table back to CSV format without polluting records with integer index labels.

title: Bidirectional Integration: NumPy Array to DataFrame and Back
code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Step 1: Create a 2D NumPy array of sensor temperatures (3 days x 2 rooms)
raw_matrix = np.array([
    [22.5, 24.1],
    [23.0, 25.2],
    [21.8, 23.9]
])

# Step 2: Convert raw array to labeled DataFrame
temp_df = pd.DataFrame(raw_matrix, columns=["Room_A", "Room_B"], index=["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"])
print("Labeled DataFrame constructed from NumPy array:")
print(temp_df)

# Step 3: Extract back as a pure continuous NumPy ndarray
matrix_back = temp_df.to_numpy()
print("\nExtracted NumPy ndarray (type:", type(matrix_back), "):")
print(matrix_back)
explanation: pd.DataFrame(matrix, columns=...) adds semantic human labels to raw numerical matrices. .to_numpy() discards labels and returns the raw C-contiguous memory buffer for scientific computing.

title: Fast Conditional Vectorization with np.where()
code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

students = pd.DataFrame({
    "Name": ["Arun", "Priya", "Rahul", "Meena"],
    "Score": [88, 94, 42, 68]
})

# Vectorized ternary: condition, value_if_true, value_if_false
students["Result"] = np.where(students["Score"] >= 50, "Pass", "Fail")
students["Tier"] = np.where(students["Score"] >= 85, "Distinction", "Standard")

print("Evaluated Student Tiers using np.where:")
print(students)
explanation: np.where(condition, x, y) provides compiled, vectorized conditional branching across Pandas columns without slow Python if-else loops.

title: Full Capstone Pipeline: Parse -> Group -> Vectorize -> Sort
code:
import io
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

raw_data = '''Employee,Dept,Salary,Rating
Arun,IT,55000,4.5
Priya,HR,48000,4.8
Rahul,IT,62000,3.9
Meena,HR,52000,4.2
Kiran,Sales,58000,4.7'''

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(raw_data))

# 1. Vectorized bonus calculation using np.where
df["BonusPct"] = np.where(df["Rating"] >= 4.5, 0.15, 0.08)
df["TotalComp"] = df["Salary"] * (1 + df["BonusPct"])

# 2. GroupBy department performance summary
dept_summary = df.groupby("Dept")["TotalComp"].mean()
print("Department Mean Total Compensation:")
print(dept_summary)

# 3. Sort employees by compensation descending
ranked = df.sort_values(by="TotalComp", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
print("\nRanked Compensation Table:")
print(ranked[["Employee", "Dept", "TotalComp"]])
explanation: Combines CSV stream parsing, NumPy conditional vectorization, Pandas grouping, and descending sorting into an executive data science pipeline.
